height: five foot four, compact and grounded
build: lean-muscled, the kind that comes from standing at a loom or kiln all day—not gym-sculpted
hair: black, thick and wavy, usually in a single braid down her back or twisted into a knot; she has a habit of pulling it loose when she's thinking
complexion: warm medium brown with golden undertones; a small beauty mark on her left collarbone that catches the light when she moves
face: an open, expressive face with a sharp jawline and wide-set dark eyes that telegraph every shift in her mood—the kind of face that has never learned to lie, where shock reads as shock and longing as longing
signature_feature: her hands—long-fingered, stained with indigo and clay, scarred across the knuckles from years of textile work; they move when she talks, and the LI is acutely aware of them
second_celebrated_feature: the hollow of her throat, visible when she tilts her head back—delicate, vulnerable, and utterly unguarded
signature_habits: she hums while working—half-remembered Tamil film songs her mother used to sing; she touches her earlobe when she's nervous or lying (a tell she's never mastered); she makes strong coffee in the mornings and forgets to drink it; she says 'amma' under her breath when frustrated, a ghost of her grandmother's voice
occupation: textile designer and small-studio owner—she hand-dyes and weaves contemporary pieces in a converted warehouse in the city; her work is gaining gallery attention but the business is still precarious

current_crisis.event: her studio's main investor—a venture capitalist who bankrolled her expansion—has just pulled funding via a cold email, citing 'portfolio realignment'; her rent is due in three weeks and she has no backup capital
current_crisis.hottest_emotion: panic threaded with shame—a feeling that she's failed, that she was naive to trust someone with her work
current_crisis.immediate_want: to find a way to save the studio without losing creative control, without having to sell her pieces to someone who will strip them of meaning

wound.core: she believes that wanting things—success, security, love—is dangerous; that reaching for them invites loss
wound.surfacing_hint: when someone offers help or attention, she flinches first, then over-explains why she doesn't need it, then quietly falls apart when they leave
